title: Ordinary resolution in characteristic zero, functorial for every smooth morphism
statement: There is one rule $R$ on all reduced schemes of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], including finite disjoint unions, assigning a finite tower $S_n\to\cdots\to S_0=S$ of ordinary blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup]. The center at each stage is a coherent ideal $I_i\subset\mathcal O_{S_i}$ (locally a finitely generated ideal); $V(I_i)$ is nonempty, nowhere dense and regular, and $S_n$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For every smooth $h:T\to S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $R(T)$ is canonically the pullback tower $h^*R(S)$ after deletion of precisely the stages with unit ideal. Pullback retains the extended ideals in their original order. The comparisons respect identities and composition; for surjective $h$ no stage is deleted.

source.place: Expose VIII, Theorem 2.3.10 restricted to finite-type Q-schemes, with tower conventions 2.1.4, 2.3.1, 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.5(i), printed pp.87,91--93. This is ordinary resolution, not the normalized toric conclusion; no Stacks tag states this characteristic-zero resolution theorem.

proof.text: Obtain L and E from [lem-trf-embedded-resolution-ambient-comparison], then I from [lem-trf-embedded-to-intrinsic-smooth-resolution]. Realize I as a finite-index smooth local rule B with [lem-trf-intrinsic-ordinary-local-rule]. Convert an isomorphic embedding to a literal closed immersion by composition. Restrict B comparisons to open immersions, which are smooth, to construct the Zariski rule A on exactly the same labeled towers. Its empty-input condition follows by transporting I.empty_input through the literal tower equality.

source.place: VIII 2.1.4--2.1.9, 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.5(ii), printed pp.87--88,91--92. Agent expansion of the finite-index realization and affine-cover interface changes in the accepted assembly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-synchronized-resolution-zariski-descent] to A, obtaining global R, its regularity/coherence/finite-type conditions and its synchronized descent on every finite affine cover. The A and B underlying labeled towers agree by construction. Apply [lem-trf-synchronized-resolution-descent-datum] to these fixed data, obtaining Datum D with that local rule and those global towers.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-descended-resolution-smooth-comparisons] to D. Its DescendedRule contains a SmoothFunctorialOrdinaryResolution, so take its rule field. The ordered contraction, extended ideals, cartesian comparisons and identity/composition/surjective-nondeletion laws are its inherited fields. Labels and the additional descent normalizations can be forgotten.
